issues.t: Airbag light from spilled drinks or seat wiring contact
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on and stays on, often after a drink was spilled near the center console.
issues.why: Liquid can drip through the parking brake opening onto the airbag computer connector, and on some cars seat material can rub the side airbag wiring. Either can stop the airbags from deploying. Hyundai recalled these cars and added a protective cover.
issues.next: Treat a lit airbag light as a safety problem. Check your VIN for both recalls and have a dealer fix it soon.

issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake warning light, or fluid wetness near a wheel.
issues.why: Certain front brake hoses could leak brake fluid, which reduces stopping power. Hyundai recalled the cars to replace them.
issues.next: Do not keep driving with a soft pedal. Check your VIN for the brake hose recall and have the brakes inspected right away.

issues.t: Front lower control arms rust through
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering steering, or a front wheel that sits at an odd angle. Visible heavy rust on the arms.
issues.why: In areas that use a lot of road salt, the front lower control arms can corrode and thin out until they crack near the ball joint. Hyundai recalled these cars to inspect and replace the arms.
issues.next: Stop driving if the front end suddenly feels loose. Check your VIN for the control arm recall and have the arms inspected.

issues.sym: Brake lights that do not come on, cruise control that will not cancel when braking, or a shifter that will not leave Park (or leaves Park without pressing the brake). Warning lights may flicker on.
issues.why: The brake light switch can work only some of the time. Several other systems rely on that switch. Hyundai issued multiple recalls to replace it.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. If they are not working, get the switch replaced right away and check your VIN for the open recalls.

issues.sym: Airbag warning light, or no warning at all. The passenger airbag may deploy when it should not, or the driver airbag may deploy harder than intended.
issues.why: Faults in the passenger occupant sensing and the driver seat position sensor could make the front airbags behave wrongly in a crash. Hyundai recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both airbag recalls and have a dealer complete them. Get any airbag light checked soon.

issues.t: ABS module can short and start a fire
issues.sym: ABS warning light, a burning smell, or smoke from under the hood, even with the car parked and off.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the anti-lock brake module and cause an electrical short. Hyundai recalled these cars and added a relay that cuts power to the module when the car is off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this fire recall. Park outside and away from buildings until the repair is done.

issues.t: Clicking or clunk from the steering column
issues.sym: A click, clunk, or light knock felt in the steering wheel when turning, mostly at low speeds and when parking.
issues.why: A rubber coupler inside the electric power steering column wears out. Hyundai extended the warranty on this part by bulletin.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the steering coupler and ask whether your car still falls under the extended coverage.

issues.t: ABS module can short and start a fire
issues.sym: ABS warning light, a burning smell, or smoke from the engine bay, even when the car is parked.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak inside the anti-lock brake control unit and cause an electrical short. Hyundai recalled these cars and told owners to park outside until fixed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the ABS fire recall. Park outdoors away from buildings until the fix is done.

issues.t: Piston slap and cylinder wall scuffing
issues.sym: A ticking or knocking from the engine, loudest when cold, sometimes with a check engine light or rising oil use.
issues.why: Pistons can rock in their bores and scuff the cylinder walls. Hyundai released bulletins with a test procedure and extended warranty coverage for short-block and long-block damage.
issues.next: Have a dealer run the engine noise test from the bulletins and ask about the extended engine coverage. Keep oil changes on time.

issues.sym: Check engine light, harsh or odd shifting, or the transmission going into a limp mode.
issues.why: The input and output speed sensors or their wiring connectors can fail. A Hyundai bulletin covers checking the harness and fitting new sensors.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask the shop to follow Hyundai bulletin 13-AT-014 before replacing the whole transmission.

issues.sym: A broken steering column cover or ignition cylinder, a car that will not start with the key, or a car that is missing.
issues.why: Many key-start versions lack an engine immobilizer, so thieves can start them without the key. Hyundai offers a free anti-theft software update and steering wheel lock through service campaigns.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for the anti-theft software campaign and get it installed. Use a steering wheel lock in the meantime.

issues.sym: A knock that rises with engine speed, oil pressure or check engine light, stalling, or loss of power.
issues.why: The connecting rod bearings in this engine can wear and fail, which can seize the engine. Hyundai added knock-detection software and extended engine coverage under a class settlement.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear a new knock. Have a dealer confirm the knock-detection software update is done and ask about the extended engine warranty.

issues.sym: Check engine light, a temperature gauge that stays low, and weak cabin heat.
issues.why: The thermostat can open too early, so the engine takes too long to warm up. Hyundai issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Have the code read and the thermostat replaced. It is not urgent, but fuel economy and heat suffer.

issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, rough idle, or shaking under acceleration.
issues.why: Some 2.0L engines set misfire codes that Hyundai addressed with a dedicated repair bulletin.
issues.next: If the light is flashing, drive gently and get it checked soon. Ask the shop to follow Hyundai bulletin 20-FL-001H.

issues.sym: Shaking or vibration when pulling away or creeping in traffic, and jerky low-speed shifts.
issues.why: The 7-speed dry dual-clutch transmission can vibrate at low speeds. Hyundai issued bulletins and updated clutch parts and software.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for the dual-clutch bulletins and software updates.

issues.t: Oil burning from faulty piston rings
issues.sym: Oil level dropping between changes, blue smoke, engine knocking, or an oil pressure light.
issues.why: Piston oil rings that were not heat-treated correctly can chip and damage the cylinders. This can lead to heavy oil use, engine seizure, and in some cases a fire. Hyundai recalled these engines.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the piston ring recall. Stop driving if the engine knocks or the oil light comes on.

issues.sym: Check engine light with transmission codes, sometimes with poor acceleration.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission can set fault codes that Hyundai fixes with a control software update, and in some cases a new transmission.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes and apply the transmission software update from the bulletin.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioner can burst in a crash
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. The danger shows only when the belt tightener fires in a crash or airbag deployment.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners can rupture instead of tightening the belt smoothly, sending metal pieces into the cabin. Hyundai recalled the cars to fit a redesigned part.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the pretensioner recall and book the repair as soon as parts are available.

issues.sym: Check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: A faulty oil pressure sensor in the continuously variable transmission can set codes. Hyundai's bulletin says to replace the sensor rather than the whole transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about Hyundai bulletin 23-AT-010H.
